svg.title: Limen credentials, audit pipeline and failure behavior
svg.desc: Four CA keys in KMS sign short-lived credentials; audit events are spooled, hash-chained and shipped to S3 and Datadog; a table shows what keeps working when each dependency is down.

text.tspan: How credentials are issued and how short they live, where every event goes, and what happens when a dependency is down
Credentials: signed by keys that never leave KMS
Every credential is short-lived and names exactly who it is for
Four CA keys in AWS KMS
kms:Sign is granted only to the control plane's role. CloudTrail records every Sign. Keys cannot be exported.
The control plane signs only after checking the ID token, the grant, and current policy
single use · stored as a hash
A stolen credential is useless within minutes. Lock or kill-session ends access sooner.
Audit: written before access is allowed to continue
At-least-once delivery, hash-chained, and fail-closed by default
its own spool is on disk.
signed by the control plane and
limen-audit-verify walks every writer's chain and reports a missing, reordered, modified or unsigned batch.
What keeps working when something is down
Running sessions are never cut by a control plane failure. New access fails closed where it must, and degrades gracefully where it can
Fail closed: needs a fresh certificate
OK if a replica serves it
OK if a replica serves it
Policy grace: proxies and workers keep using their last signed policy snapshot for 5 minutes (default), then fail closed.
